title: Mezcalita Brings Loud, Agave-Led Mexican Fiesta Dining to Indiranagar, Bengaluru
excerpt: Hindustan Times calls Mezcalita Bengaluru's brightest Mexican restaurant; reviewers point to shareable tacos, 24-hour pork ribs and an agave-led bar in Indiranagar.
body:
• Mezcalita, a Mexican cantina, is on 12th Main Road in Indiranagar, Bengaluru — No. 950, Bayt Towers, HAL 2nd Stage — and Paperboard lists it as the brand's third outpost after Mumbai.
  • Reviewers praise food built for sharing: single-piece tacos, hefty burritos, 24-hour slow-cooked pork ribs, tres leches and churros, plus an agave-led cocktail programme.
  • Paperboard puts an average meal for two at about ₹1,700 without alcohol and ₹2,100 with alcohol; EazyDiner lists Mezcalita at about ₹2,000 for two.
  • Hours listed by Paperboard are 12 noon to 1:30 a.m., all-day dining.

Hindustan Times' new review frames Mezcalita as Bengaluru's brightest Mexican restaurant — one that, in its headline's words, overwhelms, overstimulates and overjoys, and says that is the whole point. A separate review of the same Indiranagar room by Paperboard reaches a similar conclusion about the energy: it does not whisper its arrival, opening with colour, noise and mezcal on 12th Main Road.

The room

Paperboard describes a façade of arched windows, illuminated signage and bougainvillea over pink walls, with Kannada script woven into the design. Inside, the ground floor is anchored by a green bar with backlit shelves of tequila and mezcal, papel picado overhead, hand-painted tables and a terracotta staircase with Talavera-style tiles. Artwork by Mexican artist Senkoe runs through the space, according to the review.

What reviewers praise

The food, in Paperboard's account, is built for sharing rather than for quiet plating: chips with dip, loaded nachos and street-style corn arrive first, tacos are served as single pieces with a choice of masa, flour or hard shell, and burritos arrive hefty. Larger plates it names include Fideo Seco, drenched flautas and pork ribs slow-cooked for 24 hours, with tres leches and churros to finish. Vegetarian options are not treated as afterthoughts, the review says, pointing to a portobello avocado burger and cottage cheese in a torta.

EazyDiner's Bengaluru guide also ranks Mezcalita among the city's best Mexican restaurants in Indiranagar, crediting a from-scratch approach. Its must-haves for Mezcalita are Chip and Dip Mexicana, Adobo Taco, Veg Alembre Taco, Deadly Spicy Habanero Pops, Lamb Birria, Creamy Shroom Burrito, Pulled Pork Torta, Cajeta Cake and the One in a Melon drink.

The drinks

Paperboard says the bar programme is rooted in agave culture, with a cocktail menu that follows stages of tequila-making from field to fermentation to ageing. It describes drinks built on horchata with mezcal and black rice, tequila with charred bell pepper and cactus, and a peanut-butter-washed mezcal, plus Margarita Towers for groups and horchatas and agua frescas for non-drinkers. Behind the restaurant, it credits the Impresario team, with Chef Jonatan Torres Muñoz leading the kitchen.

What to know before you go

The honest caveat in the reviews is the volume itself: this is a loud, high-energy cantina by design, better suited to a group evening than a quiet dinner — Paperboard says lunch can be casual while dinner leans into theatre. Prices are premium for the neighbourhood: about ₹1,700 for two without alcohol and ₹2,100 with, on Paperboard's listing, and about ₹2,000 for two on EazyDiner's.
